== Support for newer iOS devices

- deviceConnect can now mount the Developer Disk Image (DDI) on devices running iOS 26.4 and later when the personalized DDI from Xcode does not cover the device model. In that case, deviceConnect installs the DDI from the Xcode bundle already on the host. No additional download is required.
- Devices that the personalized DDI covers continue to mount it as before.
- When Apple's signing server refuses a DDI request, the device health message now includes Apple's refusal message.
- After three consecutive failed device health checks, deviceConnect waits 30 seconds after each failure before checking again, until a check succeeds.

== Debug on private devices over virtualUSB with AI assistants

AI assistants connected to the Kobiton MCP server can now debug an app on a private Kobiton device connected to your computer over virtualUSB. Organization admins can also check and change a host machine's virtualUSB settings without leaving the conversation.

*Highlights*

- `listDevices` accepts a new `virtualUsb` filter that returns the private devices ready for virtualUSB. When you name a device that is not ready, the response explains why.
- New `listHostingMachines` tool, for organization admins: shows each host machine's virtualUSB status, the next step when virtualUSB is not ready, and its max parallel tests. Filter by device or by machine.
- New `configureHostingMachine` tool, for organization admins: enables or disables virtualUSB, chooses routing, and sets max parallel tests. The change matches the same settings in *Device Management*, including ending active virtualUSB sessions when virtualUSB is turned off.
- New `debug-device-over-vusb` skill in the `automate` plugin 1.13.0: installs the pinned virtualUSB client, connects the device so it appears in `adb` or Xcode, runs the install, reproduce, and capture-logs loop, and always disconnects the device at the end.

*Availability*

- The skill runs on macOS and Windows. Linux is not supported.
- virtualUSB works with private devices only.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc[].

== Host machine configuration in the Kobiton MCP server

- Organization admins can now configure a host machine from an AI assistant connected to the Kobiton MCP server. The new `configureHostingMachine` tool turns virtualUSB on or off, sets routing to managed by Kobiton or self-managed, and sets max parallel tests to unlimited or a custom value from 1 to 999.
- The tool applies all requested settings in one save, making the same change as the *Settings* dialog in *Device Management*. A request that matches the current configuration makes no change.
- The tool returns the machine's updated state. The response never includes the machine's IP address.
- `listHostingMachines` results now include each machine's max parallel tests setting.
- Turning virtualUSB off on a machine routed by Kobiton, or moving it to self-managed routing, ends the active virtualUSB sessions on its devices, as it does in Kobiton Portal.
- When a host machine reports `DISABLED` or `NO_NETWORK_ROUTE`, the `debug-device-over-vusb` skill offers an organization admin the option to enable virtualUSB and set routing, and asks before making the change. The skill never turns virtualUSB off or changes max parallel tests.

== virtualUSB readiness in the Kobiton MCP server

- AI assistants connected to the Kobiton MCP server can now check which private devices are ready for virtualUSB before running `vusb connect`. Pass `virtualUsb: true` to `listDevices` to list only private devices whose host machine has virtualUSB enabled and reachable.
- Each device returned with `virtualUsb: true` includes a `virtual_usb_ready` field. Pass `udid` with `virtualUsb: true` to check a specific device. A device that is not ready includes a `virtual_usb_reason` that points to the host machine settings in *Device Management*.
- A UDID that matches none of your private devices returns an empty list with a `virtual_usb_reason` explaining that the device was not found.
- virtualUSB is available on private devices only. Requests that combine `virtualUsb: true` with a `deviceGroup` of `CLOUD` or `ALL` return an error.
- Calls to `listDevices` without `virtualUsb` are unchanged.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc#_devices[Kobiton AI plugin and tools reference].

== virtualUSB host diagnostics in the Kobiton MCP server

- Organization admins can now ask an AI assistant connected to the Kobiton MCP server why a private device is not ready for virtualUSB. The new read-only `listHostingMachines` tool reports the virtualUSB status of the host machines behind your organization's private devices, with a specific cause and a next step.
- The tool reports whether virtualUSB is turned off on the host machine, no network route is configured, Kobiton-managed routing is still provisioning or failed to provision, or your organization does not have the virtualUSB add-on.
- Pass a device UDID to check only that device's host machine.
- The tool never changes machine settings and does not return IP addresses or MAC addresses.
- Organization members who call the tool receive the error `You don't have permission to do this action.` Ask an organization admin to check the host machine on the *Device Management* page in Kobiton Portal.

== Kobiton AI plugin: debug over virtualUSB

The `automate` plugin adds the `debug-device-over-vusb` skill. Describe a problem in plain language, and the skill debugs your app on a private Kobiton device over virtualUSB.

*Highlights*

- Installs the supported virtualUSB client before connecting. On macOS, the skill downloads, verifies, and unpacks the client. On Windows, the skill downloads and verifies the installer, then lists the remaining setup steps.
- Selects an online private device that is ready for virtualUSB, and asks you to confirm when more than one device matches.
- Checks known virtualUSB limitations before connecting, such as iOS 17.0 through 17.3 and iOS devices on Windows.
- Installs your build, reproduces the problem, captures device logs, and reports the results.
- Always disconnects the device when the session ends, including after a failure.
- `/automate:doctor` reports the pinned and installed virtualUSB client versions.

*Availability*

Requires `automate` plugin version 1.13.0 or later, an organization subscription that includes virtualUSB, and macOS or Windows. Linux and public devices are not supported.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc#_debug_over_virtualusb[Debug over virtualUSB].

== virtualUSB sessions

Connecting a device through virtualUSB now starts a virtualUSB session instead of retaining the device.

*Highlights*

- The device status shows *Utilizing* instead of *Retained* while connected through virtualUSB.
- virtualUSB sessions appear in the Session List, can be filtered by session type, and open to a session overview page.
- The same user can run a manual session or an Appium script alongside virtualUSB on the same device, in either order. The sessions combine into one mixed session.
- Disconnecting in virtualUSB, quitting the virtualUSB app, or terminating the session from the Portal ends the session and returns the device to *Online*.
- A virtualUSB session ends automatically after an idle period when the virtualUSB app stops sending keep-alive signals.

*Limitations*

- virtualUSB sessions do not include video, device logs, or Session Explorer details.
- Sessions that included virtualUSB cannot be converted to Test Cases.
- A CLI session started on a device connected through virtualUSB remains a separate session. Connecting virtualUSB to a device already in a CLI session is not supported.

Previously, these commands could fail with a `No active application elements` error.

=== virtualUSB for macOS

- Fixed an issue where only the most recently paired iOS 17.4 or later device connected to Xcode when several devices were connected through virtualUSB on the same Mac. Reconnecting a previously connected device no longer leaves it at *Connecting...*, and each connected device stays available in Xcode.
- Fixed an issue where a device unpaired in Xcode did not connect again through virtualUSB. virtualUSB now pairs the device again automatically when you connect it.
- virtualUSB now shows *Connecting...* until the Mac connects to the device. Previously, the device showed *Connected* before it was available in Xcode.

Update the virtualUSB app to get these fixes. After the update, a device that was paired before the update might need to be unpaired once in Xcode *Devices and Simulators*. Connect the device again, and virtualUSB pairs it automatically.

== Report access by role

- Access to the *Usage Report* and *Service Level Availability* reports is now determined by organization role. Users with the ADMIN role can view both reports. Users with the MEMBER role cannot view them, regardless of email domain.
- Viewing Service Level Availability data now requires the organization management permission.
- All other predefined reports remain visible to everyone in the organization.

// Source: KOB-55311 from PR #652
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/652

== virtualUSB automatic pairing for iOS 17.4 and later

Applies to the virtualUSB desktop app on macOS.

- virtualUSB now pairs devices running iOS 17.4 or later with the Mac automatically when the device connects, including with Xcode 27. No manual pairing step is required.
- The *Pairing* toggle has been removed from the device row.
- While pairing is in progress, the *Connection Status* column shows *Pairing...*, then *Connected* when the device is ready. If pairing does not complete, the column shows *Pairing failed*.
- Automatic pairing requires Xcode on the Mac. Without Xcode, pairing fails.
- A device that is already paired connects without pairing again. To pair a device again, disconnect it, select *Clear Pairing Data*, and then connect it.
- Android devices and devices running iOS versions earlier than 17.4 connect without a pairing step.

== iOS passcode checks

Applies to organizations with passcode mode enabled.

- When an iOS device's test runner fails to start, the device health check now reports the original error instead of a misleading passcode or certificate error. deviceConnect also no longer removes the device passcode when removing it can't resolve the failure.
- iOS devices that are not supervised by the organization now fail the health check with the reason `Cannot set passcode: the device is not supervised by this organization.` Previously, deviceConnect could set a passcode on these devices that it could not remove later. Sessions that request a passcode on these devices fail at session setup.

== Java 17 for exported scripts

Java (TestNG and JUnit) Appium scripts exported from Kobiton now target a current Java stack. Exported projects build on JDK 17 and work as modules in existing frameworks that use current Appium and Selenium versions.

*Highlights*

- Exported projects use Java 17, Appium `java-client` 10.1.1, and Selenium 4 (W3C protocol), with updated TestNG, JUnit, and helper libraries.
- Outdated dependencies with known vulnerabilities, including ReportNG, are removed.
- Test results come from standard Maven Surefire reports.
- Building and running exported Java projects requires JDK 17 or later.
- The update applies to scripts exported after this release. Previously exported projects are unchanged.

For requirements, see xref:automation-testing:scripting/auto-generate-an-appium-script.adoc#_java_project_requirements[Java project requirements].

== Minimum iOS version raised to 15

Kobiton supports devices running iOS and iPadOS 15 and later. Support for iOS 12, 13, and 14 has ended.

*Highlights*

- Kobiton rejects devices running iOS 12, 13, or 14 when they connect, instead of failing partway through a session. These devices show `UnsupportedOSVersionError` in *Device Management* and can't be used for manual or automation sessions.
- Devices running iOS 15 through iOS 27 continue to support manual and automation sessions.
- After a deviceConnect upgrade, devices running iOS 15 or later return online without manual action.

== License validation for deviceConnect

- *deviceConnect* now requires the `License.Valid=true` setting in the `dc.ini` file on each host. The setting defaults to `false`.
** New installations: add `License.Valid=true` to `dc.ini`, then restart *deviceConnect*. If the setting is missing or set to `false`, *deviceConnect* does not initialize.
** Existing hosts: hosts that already have `License.Valid=true` in `dc.ini` continue to work after the update. No action is required.

// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/643

// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/650

== Virtual device visibility in the API

- `GET /v2/devices` now returns virtual devices, such as Android emulators and iOS simulators, in a new `virtual_devices` list. Previously, the response included only private and cloud devices, so virtual devices were available only through `GET /v1/devices`. The same filters and team scoping that apply to `private_devices` also apply to `virtual_devices`. The list is empty for accounts without access to virtual devices. Existing response fields are unchanged.
- `GET /v2/devices/udid/{udid}` now returns device information for virtual devices (Android emulators and iOS simulators) that your organization can use. Previously, the request returned `404` for an online virtual device.
- `GET /v1/devices/{udid}` also returns these virtual devices. Previously, it returned `500`.
- Lookups for physical devices and unknown UDIDs are unchanged. Organizations without access to virtual devices continue to receive `404` for virtual device UDIDs.
